i tried to import a claude session just now and after the final Okay, nothing happened

The import failed. Mjolnir did report the failure, but only in the one-line footer, and that is easy to miss. This is confirmed from your dashboard log, `~/.local/share/mjolnir/logs/mj-tui-20261022T200727.077Z-1903012.log`, line 4396, logged at 20:11:05 UTC:

```
Session import failed error=resolve network source for "brokkbench26": repository "brokkbench26"
needs valid default network Git remotes for an isolated session; configure a remote or use a raw
local session: the project's Git repository has no remote; SSH and container targets clone the
project from a network remote. Add one, for example `git remote add origin https://github.com/owner/repository.git`
```

**Cause:** The `brokkbench26` repository has no Git remote. The import tried to create an isolated session, and isolated sessions on SSH or container targets clone the project from a network remote. With no remote, the import stopped before saving anything.

**Why nothing seemed to happen:** When the import fails, `mj-cli/src/dashboard/drains.rs:586-591` closes the dialog and calls `set_failure_notice("Import failed: …")`. That message goes to the shared footer bar (`Notices::set_failure`, `mj-chat/src/chat.rs:1655`). It is not a dialog. The error is several hundred characters long, so the footer probably cut most of it off. Any key press after the minimum display time also clears it. I can't tell from the log whether you saw a cut-off line or whether it had already been cleared.

**What to do:**
- Either add a remote to `brokkbench26` (`git remote add origin …`), or import into a raw local session instead of an isolated one, then import again.
- The full text is also in **"Recent messages"** in the command palette. That list keeps recent footer notices, failures included.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The dashboard has one shared footer slot for notices. Failure notices are protected from routine updates for a minimum time, but they are still one line that a key press can clear. A long, multi-clause error like this one is easy to miss there.
- The error comes from a check that runs before anything is copied: the session's source must be resolvable from the target. So a failed import leaves no partial session behind.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

**Recommendation (not done):** Show import failures in a dialog the user must dismiss, or at least keep the dialog open with the error inside it. The user just clicked "Okay" and is waiting for a result, so a footer line is the wrong place for this message. I can make that change if you want it.

**"Ignore untracked files" now has an explanation.** The import confirmation adds this line: "Ignore untracked files leaves files Git does not track out of the import. Commits, staged changes and unstaged changes are still included. Files that .gitignore excludes are never included." I checked this against the archive code: with the box checked, the import skips the list of untracked files that `.gitignore` does not exclude (`mj-checkpoint/src/archive/git.rs:1693`).

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- This dashboard has two ways to report a problem. The footer suits background events. A dialog that stays until dismissed suits a result the user is actively waiting for. Launch failures already used the dialog (`LaunchFailed`); import failures now do too.
- I did not reuse the "no Mjolnir files were changed" wording from the cancel path. A failure while saving the imported session could happen after some files were written, so the dialog only says the session was not imported.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Yes. Ryan landed it yesterday (2026-10-22). The pull brought master from `f7471b438` to `c9af4adbd`. The only new commit is Ryan's "Release 2.54.0" from today, which changes only `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock`.

The DeepSeek harness work was already on master before the pull:

- **`1bc3cfe43`: "Add DSH: BrokkAi's dsh-acp DeepSeek agent as a managed harness"**
  - Adds a profile type, `kind = "dsh"`, that runs dsh-acp 0.2.0.
  - On bare targets, it installs a pinned GitHub release binary, checked against `mj-worker/assets/dsh/runtime.json`. Linux needs glibc 2.34. The agent-dev image installs the same binary. A custom image falls back to `npx @brokkai/dsh-acp@0.2.0`.
  - It authenticates with `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`.
  - It passes the staged AGENTS.md to the agent in the `DSH_ACP_SYSTEM_PROMPT` environment variable.
  - It includes database migration 92, which is marked breaking. The old `deepseek` harness ID stays retired, so old rows from the removed harness are never read as dsh-acp sessions.
  - Ryan tested it live against a scripted DeepSeek endpoint. The test covered install, streamed turns, permission prompts, and suspend, restart and resume.
- **`b7e73c46a`: a follow-up fix.** Linux limits a single environment string to 128 KiB. Before this fix, a larger AGENTS.md made every launch fail with "Argument list too long". Mjolnir now refuses the launch with a clear message that gives the file size and the limit.

Your commit `a81e8c6bc` (deepseek-flash as the default in the DeepSeek profile example) went in between his commits. Today's 2.54.0 release is the first release that includes DSH.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Ryan gave the harness a new ID, `dsh`, instead of reusing `deepseek`. Reusing it would have made old rows from the removed harness load as dsh-acp sessions. This matches the project rule to keep old database names readable while not reusing their meaning.
- dsh-acp only accepts instructions through an environment variable or a command-line argument. Both share the Linux 128 KiB limit, so the follow-up fix refuses large files with a clear error. The other options were to cut the file short without saying so, or to fail with an unclear error.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
"the file?"

I meant the instructions file that Mjolnir stages in the DSH session's profile home: `$DSH_ACP_DATA_DIR/AGENTS.md`. It is not the AGENTS.md in the repository.

How it works (confirmed in `dsh_acp_script()`, `mj-core/src/harness_runtime.rs:159`):

- dsh-acp 0.2.0 does not read any instructions file. Before each launch, the launch script reads the staged `AGENTS.md` from the profile home and puts its contents into `DSH_ACP_SYSTEM_PROMPT`.
- If that file is larger than `DSH_ACP_INSTRUCTIONS_LIMIT` (`harness_runtime.rs:144`), the script stops before launch. That limit is 131,072 bytes minus the length of the `DSH_ACP_SYSTEM_PROMPT=` prefix and one terminating byte. The error message gives the file's path and size, and asks you to shorten `AGENTS.md` in the DSH profile home.
- If the file does not exist, the variable is set to empty. This keeps a value from the target's login shell from reaching the session.

The profile home's `AGENTS.md` likely holds Mjolnir's guidance plus your global instructions from that profile, as with the other harnesses. I did not check the staging code to confirm that. A repository's own `AGENTS.md` is a separate file. Whether dsh-acp reads the repository's file from the working directory is unknown.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The limit is the Linux per-string limit (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`, 32 pages = 128 KiB). It applies to the whole `NAME=value` string, so the code subtracts the prefix and the terminating byte.
- The check runs in the shell launch script, not in Rust. This is because the file is on the target, which may be a container or a remote machine.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

. ! status in a session should be cleared after the session is focused

Please answer the following questions.

Client: TUI dashboard (mj)
Status: Awaiting input / blocked
Other: i just know it's marked with ! (at this writing d8443f17cb24506c5ee26277fcf319f4 is an example)

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The dashboard tracks "read" status with a per-session read point (`viewed_through_event_ordinal`), not a yes/no flag. Opening a session moves that point forward to the latest event, and the change is saved as a read receipt.
- That only clears states that are worked out from unread events. A marker for a pending question or a warning may depend on other data that focusing never changes. That is the main idea the child is testing.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

A child agent is working out which state draws the `!` on session `d8443f17…` and why focusing does not clear it. I'll report back when it finishes.

The `!` on session `d8443f17…` is not a stale status. The marker is designed to stay until one of the session's child agents gets an answer to its question, and focusing the parent does not answer it. **Confirmed** from the session data and the code.

**Why it stays:**
- The parent session itself is idle. It has no pending question and no unread output. Its read point is already at the latest event (274515).
- One of its running child agents, `9645b51a…` (`6542-m1b-producer-repairs`), has an unanswered question (`elicitation-1`). The question asks whether direct negative facts can prove non-implementation on their own, or whether completeness flags must gate both branches.
- A parent row shows `!` (Waiting) when any active child has a pending question. This is on purpose. The comment at `mj-tui/src/session_view.rs:169-172` says child agents have no row of their own, so without this nothing would show that the child needs you.
- Focusing a session only moves its read point forward (`acknowledge_chat`, `mj-cli/src/dashboard.rs:1482`). It never clears questions or failures. The "mark read" notice states the same rule: "questions and failures stay flagged" (`mj-tui/src/dashboard_sessions.rs:1228`).

**A second `!` on the same row:** after the title there is a separate warning, "! Recovery copy … old". The last checkpoint failed on an unsupported untracked file type under `bifrost/.mj/lanes/6409-m4e1b/`. The last good copy is from 2026-10-22 05:00 UTC. That warning clears only after a checkpoint succeeds (`mj-tui/src/render/sessions.rs:1848`). Focusing has no effect on it either.

**My recommendation:** don't clear the marker when you focus the session. For a parent, it is the only sign that a child agent is waiting for you, so clearing it on focus would hide an open question. These changes would fix the confusion instead:
1. Make the parent row say which child has a question, for example "child 6542-m1b… has a question". `DashboardState::subagent_question` (`mj-tui/src/dashboard_sessions.rs:881`) already gets this information.
2. Use a different glyph for the recovery warning. Right now both states draw `!` (`mj-chat/src/theme.rs:747,768`).
3. Possibly: stop flagging a parent as Waiting when the child's question is non-blocking. This question says "Work can continue while you answer". Whether a non-blocking question should count as "needs you" is your call.

If you do want "seen but unanswered" to look different from "unseen", that is a larger change: it adds a third state for the row.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The dashboard works out a session's attention level from several sources: unread events, its own pending questions, failures, and its child agents' pending questions. Only the first one depends on what you have viewed.
- A row's level is the most urgent of its own state and its children's (`attention_level`, `session_view.rs:173`). So an idle parent can show Waiting because of work you can't see from its row.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Which of these changes do you want, if any? I haven't changed anything yet.
